Aro·mata·wai (n. & v.) reflection, assessing and informing.Quite literally it means ‘to pay attention to the face in the water’.

HE KUPU ARATAKI | A strong starting point

Most Boards know if something isn’t quite working.
Fewer know exactly what to change.

Perhaps the same issues keep resurfacing. Perhaps the Board is working hard but struggling to see progress. Or perhaps things are going well – and you want the confidence that your governance foundations are strong.

Many Boards will default to governance training. This helps to build knowledge and confidence, but training alone often doesn’t address the systems, relationships and structures that are holding a Board back. Training individual Board members is not the same as strengthening the long-term infrastructure of your Board.

A Governance Aromatawai looks at everything first. It shows which systems, processes, behaviours and relationships need the most attention, so that any support that follows is tailored specifically for your Board.

400+organisations have engaged our governance support
13 yearsof supporting Māori and community organisations

Some of the organisations we have supported

A Governance Aromatawai looks at:

  • Your Board’s current systems and structures
  • Your role clarity and policies suite
  • Strategic guidance and confidence
  • Board cohesion and meetings processes
  • The relationships between your Board & Manager and with external stakeholders
  • Risk controls and approach to future-proofing

The process draws on:

  • Eight dimensions of governance, through our Whare Tupuna framework
  • A survey covering 50 areas of governance
  • A thorough assessment of Board documents
  • Feedback from 1-1 interviews with Board members (if selected)
  • 500+ data points about your Board

AROMATAWAI | s42G Assessment

A governance review that satisfies the Charities Act.

For registered New Zealand charities needing to review their governance procedures. Section 42G of the Charities Act 2005 asks every registered charity to do this at least every 3 years, confirmed through your Annual Return. We review the procedures your Board has and uses against the 3 questions that the Act asks. Your Board receives a written Statement that can be adopted by resolution.

Indicative timeframeAbout 2 weeks
InvestmentNZ$2,900 + GST
Primary participantsChair, Board Secretary & TWH

What TWH provides:

  • A confirmation of your status with the Charities Register
  • A review of your governance documents and two recent Board packs
  • A governance procedures survey, confirmed by your Chair
  • A governance procedures register, with one line for each procedure
  • A signed Statement of Governance Procedures Review
  • Board resolution wording for your minutes, and one summary slide for the Board hui

Your Board will receive:

  • A plain answer to each of the 3 questions that the Act asks
  • A dated record that your Board can show an auditor or a funder
  • A review date for your Annual Return
  • A short list of matters to address, in the order we suggest
  • The date your next review is due

The s42G Assessment looks at the governance procedures your charity has and uses. It does not look at how your Board works together, how your Board relates to management and to whānau, or the capability of individual trustees. A Governance Aromatawai answers those questions, and the Whare Tupuna dimensions and Insights Dashboard further down this page belong to the Snapshot and Comprehensive Aromatawai. The s42G Assessment is not legal advice. Charities Services does not certify governance reviews, so the review remains your Board’s own and your Board records it by resolution. If a clause in your rules needs legal drafting, we name it and recommend that you engage a lawyer. Timeframes depend on timely participation.

NGĀ ĀHUATANGA | Governance themes we assess
Want to know what our Governance Aromatawai actually covers?Explore the eight dimensions of our Whare Tupuna governance framework⌄

Effective governance is more than oversight, compliance and control. From a Māori view, it is the set of leadership practices that lift the mana of the kaupapa and the organisation over time. Below are the eight governance dimensions holding the 60+ themes we assess.

Tūāpapa · Foundations

Board Charter & governance policiesValues & tikangaLegal compliance & accountabilityKaupapa Māori frameworkPolicy implementation & reviewConstitution / Trust Deed

Tekoteko · Leadership

Board understanding of rolesDelegated authoritiesRole descriptionsBoard performance evaluationTrustee preparationBoard skills matrixGovernance responsibilitiesDevelopment & trainingTrustee induction

Pou Tokomanawa · Cohesion

Board culture & wellbeingDiscussions & participationBoard communicationMeeting effectivenessKaupapa respectConflict resolutionAttendance & quorumConfidentiality & trustDecision-makingTrustee dissent

Pou Tūhono · Systems

Structure effectivenessBoard committeesCommittee Terms of ReferenceBoard packs & agendasConflicts of interestHealth & SafetyBoard administrationAnnual plansAccess to documents

Tāhuhu · Strategy

Strategic priorities & focusStrategic alignmentDecision-making frameworkStrategic plan & directionStrategy breadthThinking & discussionReview & renewal

Maihi · Performance

Governance vs operationsBoard–management relationshipKPI setting & monitoringBoard reportingFinancial management & controlsFinancial sustainabilityOperational capacityAction follow-through

Pou Tuarongo · Future-Proofing

Risk management processesRisk discussionsRisk discomfortRangatahi involvementContinuity plansSuccession planning

Mahau · Relationships

Whānau/member/community supportStakeholder communicationStakeholder involvementMana whenua relationshipsPartnerships

HE TIRO WHAKAMUA | Next steps from here

Your Aromatawai is the beginning of a journey, not the end.

Your Governance Aromatawai shows the areas for your Board to strengthen first. Following this, we can help the Board to take those steps. Below are indications of what that could include.

Governance Development⌄

Tailored training and coaching for your Board on its most pressing governance issues. This could focus on governance fundamentals, Board cohesion or governance systems, and comes with supporting tools, templates and resources.

Strategy Refresh⌄

A strong, measurable strategy that the whole Board owns. We start with the strategic thinking that your Board has already done, and strengthen this into a complete draft strategy with clear priorities and goals.

Board-Ready Indicators⌄

This turns your strategy into a comprehensive set of indicators agreed between the Board and Manager. It enables your Board to see real performance without stepping into operations.

NGĀ PĀTAI | Common questions

Questions that Boards often ask us.

Why review our governance at all?⌄

The effectiveness of governance is critical to any organisation or kaupapa. An Aromatawai gives your Board a full and independent view of how well your Board is actually doing.

It shapes specific recommendations to act on that will elevate the mana and effectiveness of your Board. Funders value Boards that review their own governance, and the Charities Act (s42G) now requires it of registered charities.

How much time will it take?⌄

The ‘Comprehensive Aromatawai’ usually takes 4–6 weeks. The ‘Snapshot’ takes 3–4 weeks.

Each participating Board member needs to spend about 2 hours: ~40–60 mins for the Governance Diagnostic survey, ~20 mins for the Personality Profile and ~60 mins for a 1-1 conversation (if interviewed). The Board debrief session is ~90 mins.

An s42G Assessment takes us about 2 weeks and asks much less of your Board. One person gathers the documents and completes the Procedures Survey, your Chair confirms the answers, and your Board considers the Statement at its next hui.

What does the Charities Act ask of our Board?⌄

Section 42G of the Charities Act 2005 asks every registered charity to review its governance procedures at least every 3 years. Your Board needs to consider 3 questions:

  • Are the procedures fit for purpose?
  • Do they help the charity achieve its charitable purpose?
  • Do they help the charity comply with the Act?

Your Annual Return then asks whether the review has been done, and the date.

Our s42G Assessment is built around those 3 questions. A ‘Snapshot’ or ‘Comprehensive Aromatawai’ also includes these questions, and looks at how your Board works together.

Which documents do you look at?⌄

We start with a check of 32 governance documents to see what your Board has in place.

Our Comprehensive Aromatawai then reviews six documents in depth:

  • Your Trust Deed / Constitution
  • Your Board Charter or Governance Manual (of governance policies)
  • Two recent Board packs
  • Your current Strategic Plan
  • Your current set of KPIs
  • Your annual budget.

Our Snapshot Aromatawai reviews two of these.

An s42G Review will read your governance documents and two recent Board packs to see which procedures are in place and in use.

Your documents are kept secure and are confidential within the Te Whare Hukahuka delivery team.

Is the review confidential?⌄

Yes. We keep all of the feedback and data confidential. Our reports and findings focus on themes raised across the Board, and we do not attribute opinion to a named person. Sensitive issues may come up and we treat them as opportunities to improve, with an independent facilitator helping to make any difficult conversations easier to have.

What if a trustee has no internet or device?⌄

They can still take part. They can sit with another trustee or the Manager to fill in the survey, complete the survey and profile with us by phone, or receive a paper copy by post with a return envelope. We can also post a paper copy of the final report if required.

How are the 1-1 conversations arranged?⌄

After we assess the surveys and document review findings, we consolidate the key questions we need to explore. Our facilitation team will then contact the particular participants that we feel we need to hear from the most and arrange the 1-1 conversations. These take place via Zoom. Each person will receive their questions beforehand to consider.

What does the Aromatawai not cover?⌄

The Aromatawai does not assess the capability of individual trustees, financial sustainability, business viability, or all legal compliance requirements of your organisation. For those matters, we recommend you engage a specialised piece of work that can be appropriately scoped.

We can add additional areas to the scope of the Aromatawai, such as an independent view on your Board member remuneration, feedback on specific policies, or extra interviews.

How do we get started?⌄

We can have a kōrero to confirm your needs. Or you could print and take the proposal to your Board. Once the Board has passed a resolution to proceed, we will begin with onboarding to confirm the engagement, timing and process.
